label: The world notices
closed_by: story-site, seeded on 27 October from the newsroom's records (state.json v0 to v3, sources.json by published date, the timeline, the compromise and impact ledgers, BREAKING-001); from Day 7 on, the desk

headline._: The story goes worldwide: 143 articles, sites dark in a dozen countries, millions of attack attempts, and still no confirmed break-in.
headline.exec: Millions of attempts, no confirmed break-in. Your three questions: do we know every PHP system, is it patched and restarted, who can pull it offline?
headline.security: Cloudflare counts millions of attempts after disclosure; 586 public proof-of-concept repositories by evening.
headline.engineer: Backports imply versions down to 7.4 are affected, whatever the subject line says.
headline.journalist: Coverage peaks (143 articles). "Millions" are attempts, not intrusions; no organisation says it was breached.

items.text: Cloudflare's CEO: thousands of attempts before disclosure, millions after.
BBC opens a live page: "Global scramble to fix critical cyber-security flaws as many websites taken offline".
Greenbone: the backports imply versions down to 7.4 are affected.
The Dutch NCSC's inventory lists 674 products: 46 known affected, 418 not yet assessed.
This site opens: 391 pages by evening, every fact linked to a saved copy of its source.
586 public php2shell repositories on GitHub; most are scanners, some are working exploits.
